# Checks, folding and resolution

What the watcher (`{{core.path}}/oncall/watch.py`) reads, how it turns signals into problems,
and when a problem changes state. The numbers are in `wikiloop.toml` under `[oncall]`; this
file says what they mean.

## Sources

| Source | Reads | Gives |
|---|---|---|
{{oncall_doc.sources_table}}

Each source reports its own health. A source that fails repeats its last answer until it
answers again, and becomes a `SOURCE-DOWN` event after
{{oncall.thresholds.source_down_after}} failed cycles in a row (one failure is usually a
hiccup of a proxy). While it is down, its problems neither resolve nor change severity, and the
report header lists it.

## Probes

Each probe covers a blind spot met in practice. When a rule starts to cover the same failure,
delete the probe rather than keep two signals for one fact.

| Probe | Catches | Query |
|---|---|---|
{{oncall_doc.probes_table}}

The restarts source, when it is on, reports `restarted`, `oom-killed` and `crash-loop` (several
restarts in the window) per container, with the last terminated reason and exit code. With
`--kube-context`, it adds the previous container's last error line, URLs and keys redacted.
Several pods that restart once on one node within the window are one `node/<node>` problem
(`node-restarts`), since a node event restarts everything on it at once. A restart is never
folded into a fleet: each pod has its own cause.

## Folding signals into problems

- **Subject.** The first of the labels `[oncall.subject] labels` names, after `aliases`. A
  signal with no subject belongs to its place: the first label of `place_labels` that is not
  in `ignore_places`. Component from the `component_label`, else the alert name's prefix
  (`component_prefixes`), else the container.
- **Problem id.** `<subject or place>/<component>`, so every alert name on one subject and
  component is one problem. A component listed in `split_components` keeps one problem per
  `variant_label` value, so two replicas or providers that fail stay apart.
- **Fleet.** One alert name on one component is re-keyed into
  `fleet/<component>/<alert name>`, listing the subjects, when
  {{oncall.thresholds.fleet_min}} or more subjects started it together: subjects are chained by
  start time, and a gap over {{oncall_doc.fleet_gap}} ends the chain. Unrelated failures that
  share a rule stay separate, so a new one is never hidden inside an old fleet. An open fleet
  keeps its members while two of them still fire and takes in a subject that started close to
  its latest member, so it does not dissolve or resolve the moment it drops under the creation
  threshold. A subject's other signals keep their own problem.
- **Severity and tier.** The highest severity among the signals that are not silenced. Tier
  and env from the signal's labels, else from `tier_of` and `env_of`; a signal with no subject
  has no tier. A probe's severity can differ per tier.
- **Text.** The alert's summary first, then what the probes add, such as a restart's last
  error line.
- **Since.** The earliest start among the problem's alerts, so a watcher started late still
  ages a long-standing problem correctly and files it as chronic after
  {{oncall_doc.chronic_after}}.

## Events and resolution

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `BASELINE` | the first cycle with no saved state: one summary line instead of one per open problem |
| `NEW` | a problem appears |
| `REOPENED` | a problem resolved within the last {{oncall_doc.resolved_kept}} comes back; it keeps its first-seen time and counts a flap |
| `ESCALATED` | the problem's severity rises; a falling severity is not an event |
| `SPREAD` | a fleet problem gains subjects; at most once every {{oncall_doc.spread_every}} per fleet, listing everything that joined since |
| `RESOLVED` | absent for {{oncall.resolve_after}} consecutive cycles, with every source that reported it answering |
| `SOURCE-DOWN`, `SOURCE-UP` | a source fails {{oncall.thresholds.source_down_after}} cycles in a row, and answers again after that |
| `HEARTBEAT` | counts every {{oncall_doc.heartbeat}}, so a silent stream can be told from a dead watcher |

Stdout tells a flapping problem once. A `REOPENED` or `ESCALATED` that brings a problem back to
an open state that stdout already told, at that severity or above, stays off it. A `RESOLVED`
within {{oncall_doc.flap_quiet}} of a `REOPENED` waits until the problem stays away that long,
then prints as `RESOLVED (away for ...)`, so the stream never ends on a resolve that the next
cycle takes back. `events.log` and the report keep every change.

The report lists the events of the cycle, then the pane's sections in order, then every open
problem that no section shows.

## Adding a probe

- **A query.** Add a `[[oncall.probes]]` table to `wikiloop.toml`: `name`, a `description` of
  the blind spot, a PromQL `query` that carries its own threshold (a quiet probe returns
  nothing), the `component`, a `severity` (a name, or tier to name with a `default`) and a
  `summary` over the series labels and `value`. Run `wikiloop build`.
- **Code.** For a check that one query cannot express, add a module under
  `extensions/oncall/` with `collect(ctx) -> list`, build each signal with `ctx.signal(...)`,
  and list it in `[oncall] extensions`. It is a source of its own, so its failure freezes only
  its problems.

Run `--once` against a throwaway `--state-dir` to see a new probe in the report before you run
the loop.
